# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later question-answering; use instead of source text)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE GHOST OF MYSTERY AIRPORT
Author: Van Powell (Gutenberg #46656). Publisher: Saalfield, 1932. Juvenile aviation mystery. Setting: Port Washington, Long Island, NY; Mystery Airport (new airport built beside a seaplane base and aircraft plant, on swamps near Little Neck Bay / Long Island Sound; Devil's Sink quicksand). July.

### Main characters
- **Garry (Garfield) Duncan**, 15, student-pilot, assistant to airport manager's nephew; practical, calm, cool, "gym-trained," studied airplane design/blueprints.
- **Chick (Chickering) Brown**, 13, impulsive, boastful then timid, fearful of dark; later brave; collects stamps (Bavarian/Venezuelan duplicates, cancelled American 2-cent stamps); wears coat with inner pocket.
- **Don McLeod**, 17, expert amateur pilot, nephew of **Bruce McLeod** (airport manager/designer, airways specialist, harassed financially; wants airline mail contract/ship-to-shore mail).
- **"Great Scott" (Scott)**, test pilot, hangar supervisor, chief test pilot of aircraft plant/seaplane base; "likes spooks"; secretly the villain; limps after claimed injury (prop flew off Dart); wears disguise; flies mail ship; dies in crash on Long Island shore after tear-gas bomb.
- **Doc Morgan**, airport handyman, herb gatherer, drinks, gossip-scatterbrain; suspected by Chick; innocent; brief "Doc" name matched pirate Morgan.
- **Toby Tew**, boatman (rents dories for crabbing), operates the Palace motion picture theatre in Winter; kindly; "Gosh-a-mighty!"/"In the name of all-possessed!"; innocent; later falsely suspected.
- **John Vance (J.V.)**, control-room chief/control tower operator, close-mouthed, black-eyed; initials on tracing; innocent (lock picked by someone else; key in his vest used by Scott).
- **Ti-O-Ga** (Indian "medicine man," Catskills/Hudson valley, Catskill town) and son **John Tioga** (~19, educated Carlisle, naval pilot cadet, actor in film "Red Blood and Blue"); son sullen, flies Dart.
- **Police Chief** (good-natured).
- **Postal Inspector** (from NY; "New York Chief" of department).
- **Smith** (mail flyer, Philadelphia run) — suspected but was false lead; Scott had impersonated/used mail flyer disguise.
- **Mr. McLeod** (Bruce); **Henry** (mechanician).
- Pilot who cracked up first (unnamed, "the first pilot"); mail pilot who crashed in swamp first night.
- **Ike** (old clam-digger, saw collision years ago).
- Control-room assistant "Chubby."

### Plot events in order
1. Ch I: Scott, Garry, Chick fly three-place Dragonfly (biplane amphibian) at night over swamp hunting "Sky Spook" ghost ship seen in luminous clouds (3-4 pilots' reports, every 7th day, July). Scott's plan: Airlane Guard; Don flies Dart (light fast two-seater, Uncle's, 17-yr-old Don).
2. Ch II: Ghost is Don in the Dart. Scott tells legend of old collision over Devil's Sink (skeleton found). Signals agreed: red Verey = spook in clouds; green = spook takes off. Scott flies Dart; Don in Dragonfly. Scott "taking off" plan.
3. Ch III: Spectre appears: two ghostly biplanes collide; mail 'plane (arriving from ship, Down-Sound, from liner catapult) apparently crashes into bay. Don flies through cloud; no crash heard.
4. Ch IV: Mail 'plane crashed in marsh. Storm. Don and Chick land Dragonfly at old boathouse/dock (Toby's). Garry & Don row dory; Chick finds **Doc Morgan** drunk in boathouse with tracing (sketch of airplane, all-metal ship); Chick accuses Doc. Strange man "the Thing that never was/Man who Never Lived" (green oilskin, slime, rubber gloves) appears, snatches envelope; Chick finds tracing still in pocket (safety pin). Chick runs. Scott arrives then leaves.
5. Ch V: Don & Garry rescue mail pilot (hurt, arm). Mail sack saved. Chick missing.
6. Ch VI: Doc says he saw "It" (green-haired thing); Chick believes Doc.
7. Ch VII–VIII: Don flies storm-tossed Dragonfly above clouds; control cable broken; Garry works elevators through floor, saves control. Landing in field near Catskill (Hudson). Chick alone at boathouse; trapdoor to dock; stamp envelope taken by man, not tracing.
8. Ch IX: Toby Tew rescues Chick; Toby identifies tracing as hull of old brigantine (India ink).
9. Ch X–XI: Farmer; Ti-O-Ga (Indian, drives Ford) treats pilot's arm; gives Garry a charm pouch (red wax swastika seal): "Keep 7 days, then open" "to clip ghost wings." Garry sleeps; dreams. Return: pilot hurt; mail delivered. Vance claims tracing (his initials J.V.). Chick ends up defending Doc; Doc said to have stolen.
10. Ch XII–XIII: Don flies mail from liner Caledonia (Liverpool pouches). Garry, Chick help; buoy pickup; record tied. Helicopter (secret) rockets, searchlight; Don's maneuvers (barrel roll, Immelmann turn). Chick sees "Thing that never was" in helicopter.
11. Ch XIV–XV: Don takes Dart back to swamp; Garry in crash boat. Helicopter lure; Garry in water; Indian John Ti (not the Demon) in helicopter; Demon escaped.
12. Ch XVI–XVII: Chick traces tracing: Doc & Vance talk about skeleton & pirate Morgan & brigantine; Chick finds tracing gone from drawer; Indian boy (John) flees car; Chick shouts. Garry & Don capture John Ti in helicopter; Vance and Chick in crash boat.
13. Ch XVIII–XIX: John's confession (father's map of pirate brig "Lady O' Fortune" in Devil's Sinkhole; Doc Morgan had visited father; mail flyer "Smith" visited home and took photo of map). Charm passes (3 yellow Palace theatre passes). Palace film shows spectre-on-smoke (Indian smoke trick).
14. Ch XX–XXI: Don tests theory: projector head in control-room locker (key in Vance's vest, found by Chick). Don flies Dart; green Verey; Chick and Garry project ghost; Don sees ghost image (Chick projects from helicopter). Sketch angles prove projection came from helicopter, not control room.
15. Ch XXII: Don and Chick take helicopter (from dock) with projector (calcium light, oxygen tank) and film; project spectre; mail 'plane (Scott flying? — actually mail flyer) nearly crashes in panic.
16. Ch XXIII–XXIV: Mail pilot angry, dives at helicopter; Garry in Dragonfly intervenes; Chick Verey signal; mail pilot's prop blast nearly disables helicopter; postal Inspector lands and summons all to appear before NY Chief at 9 AM.
17. Ch XXV–XXVI: Toby Tew calms crowd ("publicity stunt"). Scott (limping) arrives. Chick develops film (undeveloped, light-struck). Doc, Scott, Indians nearby. Dark-room bomb (smoke) steals film; Scott at window; Don/Garry fight fire; Ti-O-Ga and John search.
18. Ch XXVII–XXVIII: Chase: Dart (John) vs Dragonfly (Don). John forced to land; John said he thought Don was the man who stole map. Story of map: sailor's gift; treasure "jewels, gold, silver" in Devil's Sinkhole; Smith (mail flyer) photographed the map; Doc Morgan phoned John at theatre, revealed Smith flying mail; Doc accused.
19. Ch XXIX–XXX: Chick intensifies blue-print (camouflage map reveals Crab Channel, cross-mark by boathouse). Police chief set trap; Don, Garry, Chick; false mail pilot. Scott's trap at boathouse.
20. Ch XXXI–XXXII: Scott revealed as the Ghost ("Man who never lived") — impersonating Smith? actually disguise in oilskins; he admits he tricked all; flees with treasure chest in mail 'plane; Garry steals boat, Don chases in Dragonfly; Scott's plane crashes after Chick's tear-gas bomb falls on him; ends: "the Ghost of Mystery Airport passed."

### Key objects/items
- Dragonfly (Dragonfly, white wings, three-place amphibian, pontoon, lightning damaged).
- The Dart (red-winged two-seater, Uncle's personal property; new prop).
- Mail 'plane (Smith's); ship-to-shore mail.
- Helicopter (lift-blade + tractor prop, pontoons, rocket "gun").
- Tracing; blueprints; Verey pistol; flares; Gossport helmet tube.
- Charm pouch (3 Palace passes, "free passes").
- Projector head; calcium light; oxygen tank.
- Crash boat (electric launch).
- Chick's stamp envelope.
- Tear-gas bombs.

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE SPRING SONG
Author: Forrest Reid (Gutenberg #76205). Edward Arnold, London, 1916. Novel; setting: Ireland (Ballinreagh, Co. Irish; Rathcarragh, Ballinreagh church; "Eiffel Tower lemonade"), mid-June to late September.

### Characters
- **Griffith (Grif) Weston**, 13 (called "little boy"), sensitive, sleepwalker, sleeps with bulldog **Pouncer** (Ann mispronounces "Bouncer"); loves music, angels (Tobias & Raphael), sings; ends in sleep (last line: "But Grif slept on.").
- **Barbara** (12, prim), **Ann** (10, fat, reddish hair, freckles, mouth open, loves Palmer), **Jim** (9, fidgety, riddles, "Bun"; Grif's). **Edward** (15, fair, blue eyes, pointed chin, smoker, "Angelina" nickname, vain).
- **Palmer Dorset** (15-16, red hair, freckled, small reddish-brown eyes, Sherlock-like, reads Sherlock Holmes/Raffles; has revolver, life-preserver; shot "George"; later "I'm damned...").
- **Miss Johnson** (governess, pince-nez, writing novel *Be True, Fond Heart*, age 34).
- **Aunt Caroline** (Caroline Annesley, tall, fair, letter-writer).
- **Canon Annesley** (grandpapa, clergyman, writing book on fairies/folklore, Golden Bough, velvet cap).
- **Mr. Drummond** (curate, smooth-faced, Miss Johnson's admirer).
- **Clement Bradley** (organist; real name **Tennant**; murderer, shadow-obsessed, insane; plays Spring Song (Gian Peruzzi); burns church, leaps from tower).
- **Captain Narcissus Batt**, sisters **Miss Nancy** (kind, kisses Grif) and **Miss Jane** (very old, silent); grandson **Billy Tremaine** (William Batt Tremaine, dead at 14; flute; father drowned).
- **Doctor O'Neill** (physician, bachelor 30-35, Irish).
- **George** (circus man, "Prairie Dick"?), wounded by Palmer.
- **Johnnie** (knife-cleaner boy); **Bridget**, **Hannah** (servants); **Robert** (coachman); **Pan and Syrinx** (stable cats); **Pouncer**.
- Circus dog episode; Daniel-lion-den game with Johnnie.
- Other: Pouncer, the robin, the dragon-fly Grif saved.

### Events in order
1. Ch I: Train to grandpapa's (June). Grif, Barbara, Ann, Jim, Miss Johnson, Pouncer. Aunt Caroline meets them. Grif's sensitivity; "his strength" concerns; parents in East.
2. Ch II: Lane walk; Ann tired; Mr. Bradley (Mr. Clement Bradley, organist, "My letters" kept back). Ann and Aunt Caroline; Glebe; Grif chooses room near wood (trees).
3. Ch III: Croquet; Edward (Angelina) and Palmer arrive; Jim's riddles; Miss Johnson's novel; canon; game with grandpapa and Jim.
4. Ch IV: Night; Grif at window hears wood singing (spring song lyrics); thinks of Tobias; flute heard.
5. Ch V: Croquet tournament; Grif enters wood, finds stream, iris; garden door; the Batts (Captain Narcissus Batt & sisters); tea under cedar; Billy's room not shown.
6. Ch VI: Church; Bradley plays; Grif sees vision (old city, procession, white face); Bradley's lesson; "Spring Song" revealed.
7. Ch VII: Supper, questions; canon tells Billy Tremaine's death; Miss Johnson remarks about Grif's untruthfulness.
8. Ch VIII: Rain; Miss Johnson walks, sees naked man; Jim's Johnnie-lion incident; play *Be True, Fond Heart* performed.
9. Ch IX: Circus; Pouncer stolen by George (earrings man); Grif runs after circus at station; walks; sleeps by stream.
10. Ch X: Grif finds circus camp, rescues dogs (Pouncer), fights boy; sleeps in estate.
11. Ch XI: Inspector Dorset; Palmer and Edward ambush at shed; Palmer shoots George in leg; George confesses; doctor O'Neill.
12. Ch XII: Morning; Grif hears flute; dragon-fly; returns home.
13. Ch XIII: Grif home for dinner; cow; churchyard reading of Tobit; sees dragon in dream; Palmer seen spying at church.
14. Ch XIV: Bradley tells Grif flute is Billy's (dead boy); danger; soul theory; "Ten minutes to six."
15. Ch XV: Palmer (moth-treacle; Grif's conversation); Grif sleepwalks, Pouncer; Grif shut out; Palmer: Bradley's name is Tennant; Grif faints.
16. Ch XVI: Grif sends note via Jim to Bradley; Bradley visits; tells shadow story (murderer).
17. Ch XVII: Doctor O'Neill, Aunt Caroline; Grif's delirium; china dogs; shadow; Pouncer kills shadow.
18. Ch XVIII: Grif awakens; "three days" ill.
19. Ch XIX: Palmer and Doctor O'Neill in bower; Palmer's theory of madness; Bradley's name Tennant; gift of revolver (new) to Palmer from doctor.
20. Ch XX: Miss Johnson's birthday (34); fireworks; bonfire stopped; Doctor O'Neill summons Palmer.
21. Ch XXI: Palmer and doctor search Bradley's room; Palmer's blotter; "What are you staring at?" Bradley's shadow; Palmer's Jane story (childhood theft).
22. Ch XXII: Fire at church; Bradley plays organ; leaps from tower; dies.
23. Ch XXIII: Telegram; Bradley's history revealed; Aunt Caroline & Doctor; Grif's school plans; Doctor drives Grif; Grif's spirit fading.
24. Ch XXIV: Grif visits Batts; Miss Nancy and Billy's room; Grif recovers in her arms; falls asleep; "THE END."
